findings.explanation: The new PUT /users/<int:user_id>/role endpoint is protected only by @require_auth (app/auth.py:55-66), which accepts ANY authenticated user. The security policy (security-policy.md §2) states 'Changing a user's role requires the admin role. A user must NEVER be able to change their own role or grant themselves additional privileges,' and api-spec.md lists '/users/<id> | PUT | admin only; self-promotion forbidden'. The handler (app/routes/users.py, added lines) performs no role check and no self-promotion guard: it reads new_role from the request body and directly assigns user.role = new_role. Consequently a plain 'user' can promote themselves to 'admin' (self-privilege-escalation) and any authenticated user can change any other user's role. The required @require_role('admin') decorator (app/auth.py:69-85) is missing, and there is no check that g.current_user.id != user_id. This is a clear missing-authorization / privilege-escalation flaw.

evidence.content: Changing a user's role requires the **admin** role. A user must NEVER be able to change their own role or grant themselves additional privileges.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace @require_auth with @require_role("admin") on set_user_role, and add a self-promotion guard: if g.current_user.id == user_id: return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403. Also validate new_role against the allowed set {"user","manager","admin"} before assignment.
